decisions.title: Measure native Pi UI-prompt wait time
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 local telemetry fields. Bottom line: use Pi's native ui_prompt_start/ui_prompt_end events to measure user wait instead of relying only on ask_user tool duration. Verified project fit: ce-workflow's telemetry currently classifies user wait from ask_user calls, missing native extension prompts and dialogs. Verified upstream evidence: Pi 0.84.4 documents and exports paired UI-prompt lifecycle events with duration metadata. Benefit: complete, host-owned prompt timing and more accurate active-time metrics. Cost/risk: three small telemetry fields and two listeners; nested prompts and unfinished prompts must not double count. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now.

decisions.title: Host-owned between-tool compaction, RPC, and runtime fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit native between-tool compaction, delayed overflow recovery, RPC prompt error typing, dynamic-tool guidance, and lifecycle fixes without adding adapters. Verified project fit: ce-workflow keeps a domain-specific compaction threshold and durable continuation owner, uses Pi's public events and RPC client, and has no conflicting private runtime import. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.84.4 changelog, public RPC types, compaction and extension docs, examples, and captured 0.84.3-to-0.84.4 artifact document these package-owned changes. Benefit: safer long tool loops and runtime behavior with no duplicate owner. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no additional local code.

decisions.title: Verified private workflow generation
decisions.rationale: The official stable release is translated into the complete private nine-workflow generation with no ordinary CE runtime surface.

decisions.title: Replace the removed subagent_wait alias with bg_wait
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 prompt and telemetry rename. Bottom line: use bg_wait in generated research and creative-sidecar instructions and recognize it in wait telemetry. Verified project fit: two ce-workflow prompt generators still told agents to call subagent_wait, and the telemetry classifier plus focused fixtures used that retired name. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.64.0 changelog and public tool schema state that 0.61.0 removed the deprecated compatibility alias and bg_wait is the supported background wait tool. Benefit: generated workflows call an available tool and retain accurate wait accounting. Cost/risk: three text/fixture substitutions with no state migration. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now.

decisions.title: Package-owned watchdog, workflow, worktree, and async-run capabilities
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit 0.61.0-0.64.0 named workflow resources, workflow limits, excludeTools, session schedules, worktree providers, async recovery, progress UI, watchdog rules, and Windows launch fixes through pi-subagents without duplicating them. Verified project fit: ce-workflow already launches fixed roles through the public subagent boundary, owns its domain leases and durable evidence, and has no rejected watchdog or autoFollow settings in its project configuration. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.64.0 changelog, tool reference, configuration and extension API docs, package metadata, and captured 0.60.0-to-0.64.0 artifact document these package-owned surfaces and removal of unsupported watchdog settings. Benefit: reliability and UI improvements arrive from their owner while ce-workflow keeps one orchestration owner. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no additional local adapter or watchdog configuration.

decisions.title: Package-owned private outcome events and compatibility fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit redacted ask outcome events, Kitty repeat/release filtering, and TypeBox-shim compatibility directly from pi-ask-user. Verified project fit: ce-workflow consumes ask_user through normal tool results and lifecycle hooks, has no ask:answered or ask:cancelled listener, does not set PI_ASK_USER_EMIT_FULL_EVENTS, and does not copy the plugin schema or overlay listener. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.15.0 README, package metadata, public schema, implementation diff, and captured 0.14.0-to-0.15.0 artifact document these surfaces; the package ships no changelog. Benefit: safer event privacy and more reliable prompts without a second owner. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local event adapter or full-event opt-in.

decisions.title: Open ask_user decision context by default
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 environment default. Bottom line: set PI_ASK_USER_CONTEXT_EXPANDED=true when ce-workflow loads so decision evidence is visible without Ctrl+E. Verified project fit: ce-workflow routinely supplies decision context for planning, approvals, and recovery; the extension-level default covers every ask_user call while preserving an explicit true or false user environment preference. Verified upstream evidence: pi-ask-user 0.15.0 reads PI_ASK_USER_CONTEXT_EXPANDED at call time and supports contextExpanded as the per-call override. Benefit: actors see the full message immediately. Cost/risk: large contexts consume more terminal space. Confidence: high. Recommendation: use expanded context as ce-workflow's default.

decisions.title: Package-owned session alias command and Unicode-safe Windows broker launch
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit the /alias command and UTF-16LE Windows hidden-launcher fix from pi-intercom without a ce-workflow adapter. Verified project fit: ce-workflow does not name sessions or spawn the intercom broker, keeps pi-intercom optional, uses list-cwd only for operator discovery, and already requires exact session IDs for trust-sensitive or ambiguous coordination. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.13.0 README, package metadata, implementation diff, public command/tool behavior, and captured 0.12.1-to-0.13.0 artifact document both changes; the package ships no changelog. Benefit: users can persist a peer-friendly session name and Windows installations with non-ASCII paths launch reliably, while transport ownership stays in the plugin. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code, docs, or naming convention.

decisions.title: Name ce-workflow role sessions through /alias
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 1 optional naming policy. Bottom line: do not add alias mutation to coded role launches. Verified project fit: managed subagents already carry stable run and child identity, while delayed supervisor guidance intentionally prefers exact session IDs when identity matters. Verified upstream evidence: 0.13.0 presents /alias as a user-facing current-session command, not a subagent routing requirement. Benefit: preserves collision-resistant run identity and avoids persistent name churn. Cost/risk: operators may still set friendly aliases manually for long-lived peer sessions. Confidence: high. Recommendation: reserve /alias for user-managed peers.

decisions.title: Package-owned Markdown completion rendering and metadata refresh
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit pi-goal's Markdown rendering for accepted goal_complete results and its package/documentation refresh without a compatibility adapter. Verified project fit: ce-workflow's narrow coexistence path reads the unchanged goal-state session entry and forwards the unchanged public /goal pause and /goal resume commands; it does not render pi-goal tool results or import pi-goal internals. Verified upstream evidence: the installed 0.54.4 source, README, package metadata, and captured 0.54.3-to-0.54.4 artifact show one runtime behavior change confined to goal_complete renderResult, removal of unused piExtension lifecycle metadata, dev-dependency updates, and documentation clarification. Benefit: pi-goal users receive a readable completion card while ce-workflow coexistence stays stable. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local adapter.

decisions.title: Copy pi-goal's completion renderer into work_goal_complete
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2 tool-rendering and dependency change. Bottom line: do not add a second completion card for ce-workflow's internal terminal tool. Verified project fit: work_goal_complete already returns a bounded completion result and explicitly asks the agent to give the user one concise final summary; work-models.js currently needs no direct pi-tui import. Verified upstream evidence: 0.54.4's new renderer is scoped to pi-goal's own goal_complete result and introduces Markdown plus theme dependencies. Benefit: avoids duplicate user-visible completion output and a new direct TUI dependency. Cost/risk: the internal tool row remains plain text before the final assistant summary. Confidence: high. Recommendation: retain the existing final-response handoff.

decisions.title: Memory-bounded graph, diagnostics, and lifecycle reliability release
decisions.rationale: Grade: Adopt. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback and baseline-only edit. Bottom line: adopt installed 4.1.3 without ce-workflow source changes. Verified project fit: ce-workflow's only dedicated integration is the isolated verifier's optional read-only project_report call with compact view; immutable evidence still comes from checkpoint-scoped tools, and other durable role allowlists remain independent of this ambient extension. Verified upstream evidence: installed package metadata reports 4.1.3, and the changelog plus captured 4.1.2-to-4.1.3 artifact document the release. Benefit: inherit memory-bounded graph architecture, compact report plumbing, exact work counters, read-guard and opaque-write hardening, diagnostics bus pinning, LSP and server lifecycle fixes, and cache isolation. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure; no migration cost. Confidence: high. Recommendation: adopt now and advance only this package's reviewed baseline.
decisions.verification: Installed pi-lens package metadata and changelog report 4.1.3; captured 4.1.2-to-4.1.3 artifact reviewed; repository search confirms the optional project_report boundary and checkpoint-scoped evidence tools

decisions.title: Add optional pi-lens tools to every durable role allowlist
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: do not make durable roles depend on an optional ambient extension. Verified project fit: explicit role allowlists must remain launchable without pi-lens, while the lens verifier is selected only after a coded availability check. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.3 improves package tool internals and report plumbing but does not change ce-workflow's optional dependency boundary. Benefit: preserves role availability. Cost/risk: roles continue using native targeted reads unless pi-lens is present. Confidence: high. Recommendation: retain the current boundary.

decisions.title: Use live graph and symbol tools as immutable checkpoint evidence
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: keep immutable findings on checkpoint-scoped verifier tools. Verified project fit: project_report supplies optional orientation, while module_report and read_symbol inspect the live workspace and cannot bind findings to a recorded checkpoint. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.3 bounds graph memory and strengthens read guards but does not make live tools checkpoint readers. Benefit: avoids time-of-check/time-of-use drift. Cost/risk: checkpoint reads remain deliberately bounded. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no verifier expansion.

decisions.title: Add a ce-workflow diagnostics-bus adapter
decisions.rationale: Grade: Reject. Reversibility: Tier 2. Bottom line: do not duplicate pi-lens diagnostics lifecycle ownership. Verified project fit: ce-workflow has no diagnostics event consumer and receives bounded findings through public tool results; adding an adapter would create a second warning and persistence path. Verified upstream evidence: 4.1.3 pins the package's pilens:diagnostics publisher and subscriber surface but does not require downstream mediation. Benefit: retaining the package boundary avoids duplicate notifications and state. Cost/risk: an adapter would add event lifecycle and deduplication code without a current gap. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local change.

decisions.title: Package-owned scanners, parsers, LSP, graph, cache, telemetry, and runtime fixes
decisions.rationale: Grade: Not-our-problem. Reversibility: Tier 1 package rollback. Bottom line: inherit opaque-write recovery, read-guard hardening, parser and LSP lifecycle fixes, graph compaction and eviction, cache work counters, telemetry, test isolation, and diagnostics bus governance without adapters. Verified project fit: these are implemented behind pi-lens's public tool results and diagnostics pipeline. Benefit: avoids duplicating package internals. Cost/risk: ordinary upstream regression exposure. Confidence: high. Recommendation: no local code.
